summary: A 1932 Forest Service camp and crow's nest on Character Peak; by the 2022 visit the platform was gone, leaving two scorched trees.

facts.design: Crow's nest platform set between two trees
facts.status_note: No platform was left at the 2022 visit; two scorched trees still stand.

visit.trail_note: Listed as hike-in; there is no platform to climb.

events.note: Forest Service fire camp set up on the north end of the ridge
Crow's nest in place about the same time as the camp; year approximate
Camp and crow's nest abandoned by 1947
Kresek's book has the nest still standing as of 2010, as read by the site's authors
Deceitful Gulch Fire hit the area hard; the two trees the nest was built between were scorched at the base

evidence.supports: camp atop north end of ridge in 1932, abandoned 1947
evidence.quote: 1932: camp atop north end of ridge. Abandoned 1947.

on the Coeur d'Alene National Forest
crow's nest in place about the same time, about a quarter mile from camp

corrections.why: The 2022 visit found no platform left; only the two scorched trees remained.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Kresek's book has the nest standing in 2010; the 2022 visit found the platform gone. The site's authors suggest time or the 2021 fire.

notes_for_editor: Location: the record point (47.60944, -116.05861) matches the Idaho site pin for the nest. firelookout.com and the Forest Association index give a camp point at 47.62906, -116.05026, about 2.3 km away; not changed. Kind is 'unknown'; a tree-built nest may fit 'tree', editor's call. No staffing record. Kresek's book was not read directly; its 2010 claim is second-hand via the Idaho site.
